date_note: Activity January to October 2026; report published Nov 18.
title: Kaspersky: AuditTeam ransomware crew uses OpsAgent framework and a signed driver to kill security tools
summary: Kaspersky describes AuditTeam, a ransomware-linked group that frames its demand as an audit and consulting fee and uses the OpsAgent framework, in C++ and Rust versions. Activity runs from January to October 2026, with infections in seven countries and its leak site claiming victims in seven further countries. It kills security tools using a signed Beijing Jiangmin driver.
plain: Researchers describe a ransomware group that disguises extortion as a consulting bill and switches off antivirus using a legitimately signed driver.
exec: A newly documented ransomware group with an EDR-killing driver; signed drivers can slip past some controls.
action: Check systems against Kaspersky's published hashes, domains, IP address and file paths (such as syscache.dat and kvcore.sys); the report says shared CloudFront IPs are not reliable indicators on their own.

key_findings: Kaspersky says AuditTeam infected dozens of organisations, with victims seen in China, the Philippines, Senegal, Italy, Finland, Hong Kong and Russia, and its leak site lists victims in seven further countries.

The OpsAgent framework gives the operators file system management, process injection, privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture and network pivoting, and the ransom note demands an "Audit & Consulting fee" for a vulnerability report.
The campaign began in January 2026 and was active through October 2026 at a minimum; the page does not state how the group gets in.
OpsAgent was moved from C++ to Rust, and the Rust version uses CloudFront subdomains as C2 endpoints found through a GitHub repository.
An AV/EDR killer installs a driver disguised as a Beijing Jiangmin product and works from a kill list of about 220 process names.
recommendations: Check systems against the published stager and driver hashes, the two CloudFront domains, the IP address and the file paths such as syscache.dat and kvcore.sys.
Do not rely on the shared CloudFront IP addresses alone as indicators; the report says they cannot serve as reliable standalone IOCs.

validation.note: Original Kaspersky Securelist report read in full (read_depth full).

review.note: Compared title, summary, countries (dozens of organisations in seven countries; seven further on leak site), Jan-Oct 2026, Beijing Jiangmin signed driver, IOCs and CloudFront caveat with Securelist: match. Removed occurred_at 08:00Z, a time the page does not state.
